question: A controller must answer 404 when the service finds no course. You want a fast test that fails for one reason only. Which level fits best?
options: An end-to-end test in a real browser
A @WebMvcTest slice with the service replaced by @MockitoBean
A @SpringBootTest with a database container
A manual check after each release
explanation: The rule lives in the web layer, so a slice that starts only MVC and mocks the service checks routing and status code quickly. Higher levels add cost and more reasons to fail.

question: A test passes at noon and fails after midnight because the code calls Instant.now(). What is the most reliable fix?
options: Add a Thread.sleep before the assertion
Run the test only during the day
Pass a java.time.Clock into the class and use Clock.fixed in the test
Retry the test three times on failure
explanation: Time is an input the test must control. An injected Clock removes the dependency on the real clock, while sleeping, scheduling or retrying only hide the cause.

question: Your suite has 300 browser-driven tests, takes 50 minutes and often fails without a clear cause. What does the pyramid suggest?
options: Add more browser tests for safety
Push most rules down to unit and slice tests and keep a small set of journeys at the top
Remove all tests below the browser level
Run the browser tests in parallel and accept the failures
explanation: Each level up is slower and fails for more reasons. Rules and edge cases belong at the lowest level that can check them, and only critical journeys need a browser.

question: The API team renames a JSON field, and the Angular client breaks in production although both teams' unit tests pass. Which kind of test would have caught this early?
options: A contract test against the written API description
A unit test of the field's getter
A load test
A test of the Dockerfile
explanation: Each side's unit tests only check its own assumptions. A contract test compares them with a shared agreement, so a breaking change fails fast without an end-to-end run.

question: An integration test starts the full context with webEnvironment RANDOM_PORT. What does RANDOM_PORT do?
options: Starts a real embedded server on a random free port
Uses a mock servlet environment with no server
Disables the web layer entirely
Picks a random test to run
explanation: RANDOM_PORT loads a web application context with a real server on a random port, so tests can call it over HTTP. The default MOCK mode starts no server.

question: A UI test fails about one run in ten because it clicks a button before the list has loaded, and the team adds a two-second sleep. What is the better fix?
options: Raise the sleep to ten seconds
Disable the test
Wait for the condition, such as the list items appearing, before clicking
Run the test only on a fast machine
explanation: A fixed sleep guesses at timing and slows every run. Waiting for the actual condition is faster when the page is quick and still correct when it is slow.
